findings.description: On a denied check, tokens are refilled and stored (line 69) but updated_at is not advanced (line 73 is only reached on success). The next call computes elapsed from the old updated_at and adds refill for that whole span again on top of the already-refilled tokens. Refill is therefore double-counted, so clients get more tokens than the configured rate allows. For example, with rate 1/s, tokens 0 and a cost-5 request, polling every second makes tokens grow 1, 3, 6 instead of 1, 2, 3, and the request succeeds early. The Retry-After value is also wrong.
findings.suggestion: Set bucket.updated_at = now right after updating bucket.tokens (before the allow/deny branch), so the denial path does not re-add the same elapsed time.
findings.title: Bucket updated_at not advanced on denied requests, but refill uses stale timestamp inconsistently
